title: ALTER SCHEMA
description: Learn how to transfer a securable from one schema to another using ALTER SCHEMA.

data.text: The ALTER SCHEMA statement transfers a securable (like a table) from one schema to another within the same database.

data.title: ALTER SCHEMA Syntax
data.content: Transfers a securable to a different schema.
data.code:
ALTER SCHEMA target_schema_name
    TRANSFER [ entity_type :: ] securable_name;

items: target_schema_name is the schema you want to move the object into (cannot be SYS or INFORMATION_SCHEMA).
entity_type can be Object, Type, or XML Schema Collection (defaults to Object).
object_name is the securable you want to move.
Moving stored procedures, functions, views, or triggers does not change their schema references — you must re-create them.
Moving a table does not update references automatically — you must manually update them.

data.text: The following example transfers the dbo.offices table to the sales schema.

data.title: Transfer Table to New Schema
data.content: Creates offices table in dbo, then transfers it to sales schema.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE dbo.offices
(
    office_id      INT
    PRIMARY KEY IDENTITY, 
    office_name    NVARCHAR(40) NOT NULL, 
    office_address NVARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, 
    phone          VARCHAR(20),
);

INSERT INTO 
    dbo.offices(office_name, office_address)
VALUES
    ('Silicon Valley','400 North 1st Street, San Jose, CA 95130'),
    ('Sacramento','1070 River Dr., Sacramento, CA 95820');

ALTER SCHEMA sales TRANSFER OBJECT::dbo.offices;

data.text: After transferring, any stored procedures referencing dbo.offices will fail because the table is now sales.offices. You must update the procedure manually.

data.title: ALTER SCHEMA Key Points
points: Use ALTER SCHEMA TRANSFER to move securables between schemas.
Moving tables does not automatically update references in stored procedures or views.
You must manually update all references to reflect the new schema name.
SYS and INFORMATION_SCHEMA schemas cannot be used as target schemas.
